classification: TASK-208 both-game rc16 build (v2.00): PGO + ThinLTO, CoreGS 2.0 with the shipped shader variant list merged with the TASK-205 final mapping (644 keys, 100 new, 204 draw-state signatures). The EE library and the GS libraries carry the profile of this game's recorded scenes (the v2.00 night race at 2x and Arcade at 1x); the game is linked with GT4_HW_PGO=use and GT4_HW_THINLTO=ON, GT4_RELEASE_DISTRIBUTION=ON. The sibling Spec II executable is docs/inputs/slice419-spec2.json, with its own profile of the Spec II scenes.
purpose: TASK-208: the 1.3.0-rc16 build that ships the TASK-205 mapped variants in both games as the PGO + ThinLTO build, replacing the plain rc16 test build's executables.
status: TASK-208 both-game rc16 PGO build (PGO + ThinLTO); distribution private/slice419-dist-130-rc16-pgo (gt4.exe and gt4-spec2.exe); the packaging step builds the installer, the portable zip and the GitHub pre-release

ee_library.profile: aspect (PGO + ThinLTO: the library is compiled with the merged profile of this target, the same one the game links)
ee_library.generated_units: the rc14 hook sites on the slice217 aspect units (private/slice419-units-v200.camera360-units.json, output inventory 833876822d81729da2e642d2aff02525ef6ca960bf85b26daa77996eccbf2d90)
ee_library.recipe: private/slice419-tools/pgo419.sh: clang-cl 22.1.3, SSE4.1, the derived headers of scripts/prepare_fast_headers.py, -fprofile-generate then -fprofile-use with the merged per-target profile

gpu_renderer: CoreGS 2.0 (GT4_RENDERER=hw, GT4_HW_CORE=2), built in; gt4-gs is not part of this CoreGS 2.0 test build
release_distribution: GT4_RELEASE_DISTRIBUTION=ON: the executable loads the nine compute shaders from <executable folder>\shaders and fails with a clear message when the folder is missing
shader_cache: GT4_HW_SHADER_CACHE is set by the launcher (data\shader-cache); the launcher's --prepare-shaders --prepare-scale N compiles the shipped corpus and the recorded keys expanded over the session's CoreGS 2.0 scale (TASK-206), and a session whose scale does not match the stamp compiles nothing and records (TASK-204)

toolchain.build: CMake/Ninja VS2022 x64 ABI Windows SDK

build_recipe: private/slice419-tools/pgo419.sh v200 (the rc15 recipe scripts/coregs2_bench/pgo-all.sh with one warm shader cache per training scale): private/slice419-units-v200 (the rc15 hooked units, inventory digest 83387682...), -fprofile-generate EE library and GT4_HW_PGO=generate game, training on the v2.00 night race at 2x and Arcade at 1x, llvm-profdata merge, then the -fprofile-use EE library and the game with GT4_HW_PGO=use and GT4_HW_THINLTO=ON

owner_launch.direct: gt4.exe <reconstructed ELF> --ntsc --disc "<v2.00 ISO>" --memcard <copy>.ps2 (CoreGS 2.0, GT4_HW_SHADER_CACHE required for the TASK-204/TASK-206 behaviour); gt4-spec2.exe with the Spec II derived ELF and its disc for the second game

limits: No in-game play test of this PGO build yet: the owner tests it in game (both games); the packaging step builds the installer and the portable zip.
The profile is private and stays outside git (it holds only hashes and counts, of code translated from the game).

The list is the TASK-205 mapping (644 keys, 100 new, 204 signatures) expanded at prepare time over the session's render scale (TASK-206); the 4x gates and the identity gates against the rc15 PGO builds are the headless evidence.
The kit carries no gt4-gs package: this is a CoreGS 2.0 build and the launcher downloads gt4-gs into its data folder when the PCSX2 GS renderer is selected (decision 0070).
The prepare is mandatory for specialised pipelines: a failed or skipped prepare leaves every variant on the uber pipeline (same pixels, more fragment cost) until the next Play's prepare.

A cache prepared for another render scale is refused on purpose (the scale is in the stamp): after changing the Render scale the first session draws with uber and records, and the next Play prepares at the new scale.

A quarantined variant stays on the uber pipeline on this card and driver (its pixels are the same); the way back is deleting the shader cache folder's quarantine.bin (the launcher's support log lists it).
